body.objective: Deliver the minimum production Science Forge coordination path needed for this physics programme to replace hand-written task dispatch across five long-lived Codex-compatible workstreams. The first pilot is the black-hole workstream. A coordinator must be able to create or approve bounded work, place it in a stream queue, and see ready/active/blocked/done state. An existing agent session with valuable context must be able to pull its next work item, acquire an exclusive renewable lease, receive one complete generated work package, checkpoint or report progress, request a dependency from another stream, and close out as DONE, BLOCKED, OBSTRUCTED, or honest SHORTFALL. Reports must record the input commit, changed paths, produced commits/artifacts, checks and receipts, unresolved dependencies, scientific boundaries, and suggested next work. Coordination history must be append-only and generated views must replace concurrent edits to shared planning documents. This is a CLI-first adoption slice exposed through an installed `s-f`/`science-forge` executable; a TUI and the complete Git transaction/resource-governance layers may follow without blocking this first cutover. During the pilot, agents may continue using the repository's existing explicit-path shared-master Git discipline, but Science Forge must record and reconcile the resulting commit SHA and changed-path report.
body.stop_condition: The request is LANDED only after an end-to-end acceptance run over a clean snapshot of this repository demonstrates all of the following. (1) `s-f` is installed or invoked through one documented stable launcher and imports `planning/work-items/` plus its append-only event log with zero invalid nodes. (2) Event order is causal and deterministic: precise timestamps and/or predecessor/sequence data replace hash-order tie breaking; ambiguous concurrent transitions fail closed; the existing black-hole history resolves to its actual latest completed state rather than ACTIVE. (3) The coordinator can create a NEW black-hole pilot item with stable ID, objective, current gate, stop condition, forbidden promotions, dependencies, allowed paths, resource hint, input commit, and owner/capability. Completed objectives are not silently recycled by changing the meaning of an old item. (4) `s-f work pull --stream black-hole --agent <id>` atomically selects one ready item, acquires an exclusive renewable lease, fetches or validates the declared remote snapshot, and emits a complete work package; a second exclusive pull is rejected, while an explicitly independent-reproduction item may allow a separately typed lease. (5) The agent can run `s-f work report` or equivalent to append a progress/checkpoint record containing base/current commit, changed paths, commit/push disposition, tests with elapsed time and skipped-tier reasons, receipts/artifacts, deviations, dependencies, and next recommendation. It can then yield, block with a typed need, abort the attempt without destroying work, resume after interruption, or close out from an unambiguous `CLOSE-OUT:` marker. (6) At least one cross-stream request is created from the black-hole pilot, appears in the target inbox, is accepted or rejected with a reason, is delivered by stable artifact/receipt IDs, independently verified, and closes or unblocks the dependent work item. (7) A generated coordinator view shows all five configured workstreams, their current agents/leases, ready and active work, blockers, requests, recent reports, delivered commits, and queue depth; it must not say there is no open work while active programme work exists. (8) Work packages include every authoritative item field used by this programme, especially `current_gate`, `activates`, allowed paths, input snapshot, dependencies and `forbid`; free-text dependencies are visibly unresolved and never treated as satisfied. (9) The five agents can each pull from a distinct configured stream without editing a central mutable plan; events and source items live in sharded paths and two disjoint reports merge without manual hunk arbitration. (10) Restart the black-hole agent process between pull and report and prove lease/status recovery from committed or otherwise durable transaction state. (11) A malformed event, stale input commit, expired/conflicting lease, missing report field, and report claiming DONE without its stop-condition evidence are each rejected by negative controls. (12) The pilot produces a deterministic acceptance receipt, exact commands, a short operator guide, and an explicit list of deferred capabilities. After this run, the physics coordinator can make Science Forge authoritative for BLACK-HOLE task state while the other four streams remain in shadow mode; a second run over all five streams is the gate for programme-wide cutover.
body.forbid: using event-id/hash lexical order as a substitute for chronology; silently selecting a winner from ambiguous concurrent events; implementing only a demonstration script outside the production `s-f` path; requiring agents to discard their existing long-lived Codex context or spawning a fresh agent for every item; making all agents edit one shared roadmap or status file; treating a generated view as an editable source; mutating or deleting prior work-item/event history; broad staging, stash/reset/force-push, or ownership of pre-existing dirty files; marking free-text or stale dependencies satisfied; treating SHORTFALL as DONE; certifying a scientific claim merely because work was reported; requiring the unfinished TUI, full environment installer, or full resource governor before the CLI pilot can run; turning the advisory Science Forge CI rail into a required repository-wide exhaustive replay; claiming five-agent production readiness from a single happy-path pull without concurrency, crash-recovery, dependency-request, and negative-control tests.
notes: 2026-07-19 physics coordinator: This request is the adoption gate for task distribution and organization, not a request to finish the entire Science Forge specification. Preserve the useful context of five long-lived Codex sessions: each session pulls work for its configured stream and reports/checkpoints back into the graph.

2026-07-19 physics coordinator: Use black-hole as the first pilot because its prior objective is complete and a fresh follow-on item can test correct create/pull/lease/report semantics without changing the meaning of the completed item. Keep the other four streams advisory until the pilot acceptance receipt passes.

2026-07-19 observed integration defect: `sfc import-program` imported the present queue as 57 nodes with zero invalid items, but `sfc context` and `sfc work-package` reported `sf:program/work/black-hole` as ACTIVE even though a later DONE event records completion. All transitions used the date 2026-07-19 and the fold chose max `(when,id)`, so content-address hash order overrode chronology. The same generated context also printed `No open work items` while listing ACTIVE programme items, and the generated package omitted authoritative fields including `current_gate`. These are mandatory pilot repairs, not cosmetic improvements.

2026-07-19 scope boundary: For the first cutover, existing repository Git commands remain permitted under AGENTS.md shared-master discipline. The agent report must nevertheless capture base/current commits, explicit changed paths, checks and push disposition. The later `s-f add/check/commit/sync/publish` transaction layer can replace those commands incrementally after task orchestration is trustworthy.
